message.content:
Los Angeles (Pacific Time) is **9 hours behind** Berlin (Central European Time).  
So when it’s noon in Los Angeles, it’s 9 p.m. in Berlin.  

*(Both cities observe daylight‑saving time, but the offset stays constant at 9 hours throughout the year.)*

We can compute based on standard offsets: Los Angeles is Pacific Time (UTC-8 or UTC-7 during DST). Berlin is Central European Time (UTC+1 or UTC+2 during DST). The difference depends on whether both are observing daylight saving time. Typically, Los Angeles is UTC-7 during DST (summer), Berlin is UTC+2 during DST. So difference is 9 hours. During winter, LA is UTC-8, Berlin is UTC+1, difference is 9 hours as well. Wait, check: In winter, LA is UTC-8, Berlin is UTC+1, difference is 9 hours. In summer, LA is UTC-7, Berlin is UTC+2, difference is also 9 hours. Actually, the difference remains 9 hours all year round because both observe DST simultaneously but offset changes by one hour each. So the time difference is always 9 hours.
